A 2022 iScience tail-tracking study (PMC9356099), for whose left and right is meant: angles are "relative to the body axis", and the wag leaned "toward the right side of the dog's body axis when facing the dog's owner"; https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9356099/

title: Your Dog's Tail Wag May Lean to Its Right When It Sees You 🐕 (Things Living In Your House #67)
description:
Dog tail wag meaning: what does it mean when a dog wags its tail more to the left or the right? A 2024 review in Biology Letters says wagging is lopsided: dogs lean the wag to their own right for things they like, such as their owner, and to their own left for things that make them pull back, such as an unfamiliar, dominant dog. In a 2013 study, dogs watching videos of a left-leaning wag had higher heart activity and acted more anxious than with a right-leaning wag. It is a lean, not a rule: wagging goes with good and bad excitement, and a robot-dog study did not fit the simple story. A wagging tail does not always mean a dog is friendly.
